titulo.texto: Casa Boker: The Steel Hardware Store Inaugurated by Porfirio Díaz

frase_gancho.texto: The staircase of the Casa Boker is not in the Casa Boker: today it is the entrance stairway of the Government Palace in Xalapa.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue along Dieciséis de Septiembre Avenue toward the east, until you reach the great plaza of the Zócalo.

como_llegar.texto: Continue along Isabel la Católica toward Dieciséis de Septiembre Avenue, where the Casa Boker stands, a building with a metal frame that housed a historic hardware store.

guion_corto.texto: The grand staircase of this building is not here, but in Xalapa. The government of Veracruz bought it in nineteen oh eight, and today it serves as the entrance to that city’s Government Palace. The building that once had it is the Casa Boker. Porfirio Díaz inaugurated it on the third of July, nineteen hundred, with a structure of metal columns and beams designed by architects from New York. Roberto Boker, who had come from Germany, had opened his first store on the first of November, eighteen sixty-five. The hardware store closed in December two thousand twenty-four, but the Boker name still stands on the facade.

guion_largo.texto:
Before this building existed, the Boker name was already selling tools in Mexico. Roberto Boker was originally from Remscheid, in Germany, where his family had been making and selling tools for centuries. On the first of November, eighteen sixty-five, he opened his first store, Roberto Boker y Compañía, when Maximilian of Habsburg ruled the country.

The building in front of you came thirty-five years later. Porfirio Díaz inaugurated it on the third of July, nineteen hundred. It was designed by the firm De Lemos and Cordes, of New York, which also built the first Macy’s stores. The Mexican engineer Gonzalo Garita took part in the construction. He also worked with that firm on the [Banco de México](cdmx_15_banco_mexico) building, another stop on your tour.

The novelty was in the structure. It was one of the first buildings in the country built with metal columns and beams, and in its day it was among the most modern. It was a large store on three levels, where they sold hardware, notions, cutlery, tools for farming and mining, and household goods. Among the most famous products were Singer sewing machines.

Now, the fact that gives this stop its title. A monumental staircase connected the ground floor with the next level, in the west courtyard. The company itself tells that, in nineteen oh eight, it was sold to the government of Veracruz. Today it is the entrance stairway of the Government Palace in Xalapa. It shows how the pieces of a building can travel across the country.

The building also survived disasters. A fire, on the eighth of February, nineteen seventy-five, made it necessary to reinforce the columns from the foundations and the beams with steel rods. In those years, earthquake-resistant joints were added, and that reinforcement helped the building withstand the earthquakes of September nineteen eighty-five. In nineteen seventy-six, part of the building was rented to Sanborns. That branch closed in August two thousand twenty-four.

The hardware store was in the hands of the family’s fourth generation. It closed in December two thousand twenty-four, after one hundred fifty-nine years of service. Many tourist guides still describe it as a place you can visit inside. For that reason, on this tour, the Casa Boker is narrated from the street. What you can see is its facade, with the Boker name and a characteristic green color, and the volume of the building on the corner.

This end of the Madero area leaves you with one idea. Between eighteen sixty-five and nineteen hundred, this family went from a single store to a great building designed in New York. It shows how commerce and outside investment changed the face of the Centro in the early twentieth century.

Now it is time to reach the Zócalo. You leave behind the shops of the Porfirian era. Ahead lies the central plaza of the capital, where many centuries of history cross paths.

texto.Key fact: the hardware store closed in December 2024

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Casa Boker is still operating as a hardware store that you can visit inside.
texto.respuesta: Reality: The hardware store closed in December two thousand twenty-four after one hundred fifty-nine years, and the Sanborns in the building closed in August of that year; some tourist guides still describe it as open to visitors.
